page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an AMD EPYC 7571 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 384 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It also integrates 1,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance store and provides a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps. Accelerated graphics hardware is absent, with 0 GPUs available.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct performance characteristics governed by the older Zen-generation AMD architecture. In single-threaded tasks, the instance scores in the bottom 10%, recording 727.0 in Geekbench and 591.29 in stress-ng single-core tests. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded throughput settles in the middle tier, yielding a multi-core Geekbench score of 6,913.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 30,316.6. Hardware-assisted cryptographic workloads perform in the top 25%, reaching 38,785.42 on PassMark encryption tests thanks to dedicated AES and SHA instruction sets.

Data handling and memory throughput show balanced performance across sustained operations. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 81.48 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 38.9 GB/sec. In database evaluations, the server registers 11,314.22 operations on PassMark and 29.18 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. The inclusion of bundled 1,800 GB NVMe local storage provides qualitative cost advantages for I/O-intensive workloads, eliminating external storage throughput overhead for scratch disks or transient caches.

The primary tradeoff of the r5ad.12xlarge is modest single-thread execution speed balanced against significant memory capacity and low-latency local storage. Consequently, the instance is well suited for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, transactional databases requiring high-speed scratch space, big data processing, and enterprise batch jobs.
description: Amazon Web Services r5ad.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 384 GB of DDR4 memory paired with 1,800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate moderate multi-threaded compute capability and high cryptographic throughput via hardware AES and SHA instructions, balanced against modest single-core execution speeds. Memory read bandwidth reaches 81.48 GB/sec for uncached blocks, supporting operations like Redis SET at 29.18 million operations per second. Lacking dedicated GPU hardware, the instance balances dense RAM allocation and fast local scratch storage without additional storage volume overhead. It is appropriately configured for memory-intensive workloads including in-memory caching systems, distributed data processing, operational relational databases, and enterprise data analytics pipelines.
